stories.title: Suno to add watermarks to AI-generated songs amid ongoing copyright lawsuits
stories.summary: AI music generator Suno says it will start watermarking AI-generated tracks to make them easier to identify, part of an effort to curb spammy AI music flooding platforms. The move comes as the company continues to fight legal battles brought by the recording industry over how it trained its models.
stories.whyItMatters: It's an early attempt at provenance standards for AI-generated media, arriving while Suno's underlying legal fight over copyrighted training data is still unresolved.
whatToWatch: How Suno's watermarking works and whether it can be stripped or bypassed
Outcome of the ongoing lawsuits against Suno
Whether streaming platforms adopt the watermarks to label or filter AI music
questions: Does watermarking address labels' underlying copyright claims, or just spam concerns?
Will other AI music generators follow suit?

stories.title: Ford unveils 'Fathom,' a midsize electric pickup starting at $28,350
stories.summary: Ford has named and priced its first midsize electric pickup truck: the Fathom, starting at $28,350. The launch positions the truck as a lower-cost EV option in a segment where affordability has been a sticking point for buyers.
stories.whyItMatters: The aggressive starting price is a bet that cheaper EVs can revive demand at a time when EV sales growth has cooled and automakers are under pressure to compete on cost.

On-sale date and initial order volume
Competing responses from other automakers' affordable EV trucks
questions: What range and towing capacity does the base Fathom offer?

stories.title: OpenAI's rumored ring-shaped smart speaker could cost $300–$400
stories.summary: Reports say OpenAI is working on an AI-powered, ring-shaped smart speaker that could be priced between $300 and $400. If accurate, it would mark OpenAI's most concrete step yet into consumer hardware.
stories.whyItMatters: A hardware push would put OpenAI in direct competition with Amazon, Google, and Apple's home devices, extending ChatGPT's reach beyond apps and into physical products.

stories.title: Wired: the 'hottest new AI chatbot' is actually a person answering your questions
stories.summary: Wired reports on a viral service marketed as a cutting-edge AI chatbot that turns out to be staffed by a human answering user questions directly, spotlighting confusion over what actually counts as "AI" in consumer products.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a pointed example of the broader scrutiny over AI-washing, where products are marketed as AI-driven even when human labor is doing the real work behind the scenes.

stories.title: Meta ordered to pay additional $567 million in public nuisance ruling
stories.summary: A court has ordered Meta to pay an additional $567 million in a public nuisance case, adding to the company's growing pile of legal costs tied to harms linked to its platforms.
stories.whyItMatters: It's part of a widening pattern of courts holding platforms financially liable for the societal effects of their products, a precedent other plaintiffs could point to in future suits.

stories.title: Google warns hackers are calling financial-firm employees to gain access and extort victims
stories.summary: Google says attackers are using phone calls to trick employees at financial firms into granting system access, which they then use to steal data and extort victims. The warning points to social engineering, rather than purely technical exploits, as a growing entry point for breaches.
stories.whyItMatters: It highlights a rising attack vector against the financial sector that bypasses conventional credential and technical defenses, relying instead on tricking employees directly.

Guidance from Google or other security researchers on defending against these calls
questions: Which threat group is behind these calls?
